Marathon Petroleum has climbed 9.6% over two weeks and gained another 0.7% today, riding a sharp rally since September 11th. The move reflects a tightening physical oil market: U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel while world crude sits at $130.80—a $23.80 gap that signals regional supply stress—and refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, near maximum. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown, combined with ongoing Houthi attacks and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, has constrained crude supply globally, which typically boosts margins for U.S. refiners who benefit when crude prices rise relative to refined product values.

The stock's momentum also reflects that U.S. crude has pulled back from earlier highs (falling below $100 this week on diplomatic signals) while the world price remains elevated, giving American refiners access to cheaper feedstock relative to global competitors. This supply disruption and price divergence is exactly the environment that tends to benefit domestic refining operations.
